key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves next-step CFD surrogate prediction by combining multiscale spectral encoding, PDE-aware attention, and self-supervised physics pretraining to better recover localized flow structures.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster surrogate modeling option for real-world fluid simulations where accurate reconstruction of wakes, near-body flow, and other multiscale features is critical.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding for multiscale flow representation
Physics-biased self-attention guided by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining via Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Across cylinder-wake and fluid-structure-interaction benchmarks, the model achieved the best aggregate accuracy, including 0.05875 all-channel NMSE and 0.97019 Pearson correlation on cylinder wake, plus 2.70×10^-4 all-channel NMSE on FSI.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on two benchmark cases, so robustness and cost-benefit tradeoffs may still need validation on broader geometries, boundary conditions, and longer rollout horizons.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
